heading: Life-Cycle Funds vs. DIY Portfolio: Automate or Manage Investing?
tldr: Life-cycle mutual funds automatically adjust your asset allocation, becoming more conservative as your goal approaches.
A Do-It-Yourself (DIY) portfolio requires you to actively manage and rebalance your investments across equity, debt, and other assets.
Life-cycle funds offer convenience and professional rebalancing, ideal for those who prefer a hands-off approach.
DIY portfolios provide greater control, customisation, and potentially lower expense ratios, but demand time and expertise.
The choice depends on your investment knowledge, willingness to actively manage, and preference for automation versus control.
caption:
Life-Cycle Funds vs. DIY Portfolio: Automate or Manage Investing?. In simple terms: Life-cycle mutual funds automatically adjust your asset allocation, becoming more conservative as your goal approaches. We broke this down in plain English so you can see exactly what it means for your money — and what to do about it. Give it a read.
